WhyWatt — Solar Yield Review for a ZIP (PVWatts)¶

Purpose: see the solar table WhyWatt will use for a ZIP — built offline from NREL/NLR PVWatts v8 (data/solar/pvwatts_zip.json, see docs/OfflineSolarData_Plan.md). Everything is for a 1 kW DC system at the default orientation (fixed roof mount, 20° tilt, facing south, 14% losses); multiply by system size (panels × kW/panel) for a real home.

  1. Monthly — sunlight on the panel (radiation) and the energy a 1 kW system produces.
  2. Average day — for each month, the hour-by-hour output on an average day (12 curves).
  3. ZIP vs zone fallback — how much the ZIP-level table differs from the CEC-zone table it replaces.

Set ZIP in the next section and run all cells. Run on the WhyWatt (venv) kernel. Reads only committed data — no network, no API key.

In [1]:
import json, calendar
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, matplotlib.pyplot as plt, matplotlib as mpl
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D

ROOT = Path.cwd().parent if Path.cwd().name == 'notebooks' else Path.cwd()
PV  = json.loads((ROOT/'data/solar/pvwatts_zip.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
REG = json.loads((ROOT/'data/solar/regions.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
Z2Z = json.loads((ROOT/'data/climate/zip_to_zone.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8'))

MONTHS = [calendar.month_abbr[m] for m in range(1, 13)]
DAYS   = np.array([calendar.monthrange(2025, m)[1] for m in range(1, 13)])
DST    = np.array([m in range(3, 11) for m in range(1, 13)])   # Mar–Oct mostly on daylight time
PEAK   = (16, 21)                                               # 4–9pm clock time

# Chart tokens (light). Single-series panels take categorical slots 1–2; the month curves use
# the blue ordinal ramp (steps 250→700), darkest at the June solstice.
INK, INK2, MUTED, GRID = '#0b0b0b', '#52514e', '#8a8984', '#e4e3df'
ENERGY, SUN, REF, PEAKFILL = '#2a78d6', '#eb6834', '#9c9b96', '#f3f2ee'
RAMP = {0: '#0d366b', 1: '#184f95', 2: '#1c5cab', 3: '#2a78d6', 4: '#5598e7', 5: '#6da7ec', 6: '#86b6ef'}
def month_color(m):   # m = 0..11; distance (in months) from June
    return RAMP[min(abs(m - 5), 12 - abs(m - 5))]
def month_style(m):   # rising sun (Jan–Jun) solid, falling (Jul–Dec) dashed
    return '-' if m <= 5 else (0, (4, 2))

mpl.rcParams.update({'figure.dpi': 110, 'font.size': 10, 'axes.edgecolor': MUTED,
    'axes.labelcolor': INK2, 'xtick.color': INK2, 'ytick.color': INK2, 'text.color': INK,
    'axes.grid': True, 'grid.color': GRID, 'grid.linewidth': .8, 'axes.axisbelow': True,
    'axes.spines.top': False, 'axes.spines.right': False, 'axes.titlelocation': 'left',
    'axes.titlesize': 11, 'axes.titleweight': 'bold'})

def resolve(zipcode):
    """ZIP → (site, level, label): ZIP-level table, else CEC-zone station, else CZ4 default."""
    z = str(zipcode).strip()
    if z in PV['zips']:
        e = PV['zips'][z]
        return PV['sites'][e['site']], 'zip', f"ZIP-level table (region: {REG[e['region']]['name']})"
    zone = Z2Z.get(z)
    if zone in PV['zones']:
        return PV['sites'][PV['zones'][zone]['site']], 'zone', f'not harvested yet → {zone} zone-station table'
    return PV['sites'][PV['default']['site']], 'default', 'unknown ZIP → CZ4 (San José) default table'

def avg_day(site):
    """12×24 kWh per hour on an average day of each month, per 1 kW — in CLOCK time."""
    lst = np.array(site['intraday_shape']) * (np.array(site['ac_monthly']) / DAYS)[:, None]
    return np.array([np.roll(row, 1) if dst else row for row, dst in zip(lst, DST)])

print(f"{len(PV['zips'])} ZIP-level tables · regions: "
      + ', '.join(f"{r['tag']} (wave {r['wave']}, {r['sites']} sites)" for r in PV['_meta']['regions']))

29 ZIP-level tables · regions: ca_zone_stations (wave 0, 16 sites), svce (wave 1, 29 sites)

Choose a ZIP¶

Harvested so far: SVCE (e.g. Mountain View 94040, Cupertino 95014, Gilroy 95020, Mt. Hamilton 95140). Any other California ZIP falls back to its CEC-zone table; an unknown ZIP falls back to San José (CZ4).

1. Monthly radiation and energy (1 kW system)¶

Top: sunlight reaching the tilted panel face (plane-of-array irradiation, kWh per m² per month). Bottom: AC energy a 1 kW system delivers (kWh per month). Separate panels because they are different quantities — the energy bars track the radiation bars, minus conversion and system losses.

In [3]:
def plot_monthly(site, title):
    poa, ac = np.array(site['poa_monthly']), np.array(site['ac_monthly'])
    fig, (a1, a2) = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(9, 6.2), sharex=True, gridspec_kw={'hspace': .45})
    x = np.arange(12)
    for ax, vals, color, name, unit, total in [
            (a1, poa, SUN, 'Radiation on the panel', 'kWh/m² per month', poa.sum()),
            (a2, ac, ENERGY, 'Energy from a 1 kW system', 'kWh per month', ac.sum())]:
        ax.bar(x, vals, width=.72, color=color, edgecolor='white', linewidth=2)
        ax.set_title(f'{name}  —  {total:,.0f} {unit.split(" per")[0]} / year', pad=8)
        ax.set_ylabel(unit); ax.grid(axis='x', visible=False)
        for i in (int(vals.argmax()), int(vals.argmin())):          # selective labels: max & min
            ax.annotate(f'{vals[i]:.0f}', (i, vals[i]), xytext=(0, 3), textcoords='offset points',
                        ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=9, color=INK2)
        ax.set_ylim(0, vals.max() * 1.15)
    a2.set_xticks(x, MONTHS)
    fig.suptitle(title, x=.125, ha='left', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold', y=.99)
    plt.show()

plot_monthly(SITE, f'ZIP {ZIP} — monthly solar (1 kW DC, default orientation)')

2. Average day for each month (1 kW system)¶

Each curve is one month's average day: the energy produced in each hour (kWh in that hour = average kW). Hours are clock time — PVWatts reports standard time, so March–October are shifted one hour for daylight saving. The shaded band is the 4–9pm peak: the solar output that lands there is small, which is why a battery (charged at midday, discharged 4–9pm) matters. Darker = closer to the June solstice; Jan–Jun solid, Jul–Dec dashed.

In [4]:
def plot_avg_day(site, title):
    day = avg_day(site)
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9.5, 5.2))
    ax.axvspan(PEAK[0], PEAK[1], color=PEAKFILL, zorder=0)
    ax.text(PEAK[0] + .15, day.max() * 1.07, '4–9pm peak', color=INK2, fontsize=9, va='top')
    hours = np.arange(24)
    for m in range(12):
        ax.plot(hours, day[m], color=month_color(m), ls=month_style(m), lw=2, label=MONTHS[m],
                solid_capstyle='round')
    for m in (5, 11):                                                   # direct labels: Jun, Dec
        h = int(day[m].argmax())
        ax.annotate(MONTHS[m], (h, day[m, h]), xytext=(0, 5), textcoords='offset points',
                    ha='center', fontsize=9, color=INK, fontweight='bold')
    ax.set_xticks(range(0, 25, 3), [f'{h % 12 or 12}{"am" if h % 24 < 12 else "pm"}' for h in range(0, 25, 3)])
    ax.set_xlim(4, 21); ax.set_ylim(0, day.max() * 1.12)
    ax.set_xlabel('hour of day (clock time)'); ax.set_ylabel('kWh in the hour  (= average kW)')
    ax.set_title(title, pad=10)
    ax.legend(ncol=2, frameon=False, fontsize=9, loc='upper left', bbox_to_anchor=(1.01, 1),
              title='month', title_fontsize=9, handlelength=2.4)
    plt.show()
    peak_share = np.array([day[m, PEAK[0]:PEAK[1]].sum() / day[m].sum() for m in range(12)])
    return pd.DataFrame({'kWh/day (avg day)': day.sum(1), 'peak hour output kW': day.max(1),
                         'share in 4–9pm': peak_share}, index=MONTHS).T

plot_avg_day(SITE, f'ZIP {ZIP} — average day by month (1 kW DC)').style.format('{:.2f}').format(
    '{:.1%}', subset=pd.IndexSlice['share in 4–9pm', :])

3. ZIP-level table vs the zone fallback¶

Only meaningful for a harvested ZIP. Each panel is one month's average day: blue = this ZIP's table, gray = the CEC-zone station table that any un-harvested ZIP in the zone would use.

Read the annual difference, not single months. PVWatts weather is a typical meteorological year (TMY) per ~4 km weather cell, stitched month-by-month from different historical years. Two nearby cells can pick a cloudier February from different years, so single months can differ by 5–12% even when the annual totals match within 1%.

In [5]:
def plot_vs_zone(site, zone_site, title):
    a, b = avg_day(site), avg_day(zone_site)
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(3, 4, figsize=(11, 6.6), sharex=True, sharey=True)
    for m, ax in enumerate(axes.flat):
        ax.axvspan(*PEAK, color=PEAKFILL, zorder=0)
        ax.plot(range(24), b[m], color=REF, lw=2)
        ax.plot(range(24), a[m], color=ENERGY, lw=2)
        d = a[m].sum() / b[m].sum() - 1
        ax.set_title(f'{MONTHS[m]}  {d:+.1%}', fontsize=9.5, fontweight='normal', color=INK)
        ax.set_xlim(4, 21); ax.set_xticks([6, 12, 18], ['6am', 'noon', '6pm'])
    fig.legend([Line2D([], [], color=ENERGY, lw=2), Line2D([], [], color=REF, lw=2)],
               ['this ZIP', 'zone fallback'], loc='upper right', ncol=2, frameon=False)
    fig.suptitle(title, x=.07, ha='left', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
    fig.supylabel('kWh in the hour (1 kW)', color=INK2, fontsize=9.5)
    fig.tight_layout(); plt.show()

if LEVEL == 'zip':
    plot_vs_zone(SITE, ZONE_SITE, f'ZIP {ZIP} vs {zone} zone table — average day, % = daily energy difference')
else:
    print(f'ZIP {ZIP} has no ZIP-level table yet — it uses the {zone} zone table directly.')

rows = []
for z, e in PV['zips'].items():
    s, zs = PV['sites'][e['site']], PV['sites'][PV['zones'][e['zone']]['site']]
    jul = avg_day(s)[6]
    rows.append({'ZIP': z, 'region': e['region'], 'zone': e['zone'],
                 'selected because': REG[e['region']]['zips'][z]['reason'],
                 'kWh/kW/yr': s['ac_annual'], 'vs zone': s['ac_annual'] / zs['ac_annual'] - 1,
                 '4 kW kWh/yr': 4 * s['ac_annual'], 'Jul 4–9pm share': jul[PEAK[0]:PEAK[1]].sum() / jul.sum()})
df = pd.DataFrame(rows).sort_values('vs zone').reset_index(drop=True)
df.style.format({'kWh/kW/yr': '{:,.0f}', '4 kW kWh/yr': '{:,.0f}', 'vs zone': '{:+.1%}',
                 'Jul 4–9pm share': '{:.1%}'})

Try it live (optional)¶

Interactive ZIP box — works in Jupyter, not in the exported HTML.

In [7]:
from ipywidgets import interact, Text
def live(zipcode='95140'):
    s, level, how = resolve(zipcode)
    print(f'ZIP {zipcode}: {how} · {s["ac_annual"]:,.0f} kWh/kW/yr')
    plot_monthly(s, f'ZIP {zipcode} — monthly solar (1 kW)')
    plot_avg_day(s, f'ZIP {zipcode} — average day by month (1 kW)')
interact(live, zipcode=Text('95140', description='ZIP'));
